Small-cap financials (ABDA, YULE, BEKS, LPGI) are seeing speculative retail inflows, creating volatility that institutional investors should exploit via selective entry, not blanket exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to XCIS, LIFE, and ASMI on idiosyncratic catalysts, but keep overall financials underweight vs. index. The sector's flat aggregate masks a bifurcated tape: Indonesian names are outperforming US peers, yet the NORMAL signal argues against chasing broad beta. Rotate into high-momentum insurers and niche lenders, and trim laggards like BTPS if they fail to hold gains.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US IPPs are structurally re-rated by hyperscaler PPA demand, making contracted power the cleanest AI-infrastructure play through 2026.
Indonesia's captive renewable market (industrial estates, mining) is a durable growth vector as PLN grid bottlenecks push off-takers to self-generation.
Climate-tech equipment makers face margin compression from subsidy phase-outs, while asset owners with long-term PPAs capture the risk-adjusted upside.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US IPPs (NRG, CEG, VST) on AI-driven power demand and tight supply; Indonesia renewables (POWR, PKPK) offer steady upside from captive industrial and geothermal pipelines. Rotate out of hydrogen/equipment names like PLUG. Favor contracted cash flows over merchant volatility; monitor US rate cuts for refinancing tailwinds.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Domestic consumption resilience is decoupling from global FMCG weakness, driven by stable Indonesian purchasing power and government social-spending programs that support staple demand.
Small/mid-cap consumer names (FOLK, SURI, KING) are leading on differentiated product innovation and distribution expansion into tier-2/3 cities, creating durable share-gain stories.
Subsector rotation favors discretionary-adjacent FMCG (BIKE, MGLV) over pure staples as urban wage growth and e-commerce penetration lift premium and convenience segments.
sectors.ai: Buy selective FMCG laggards with domestic revenue exposure (FOLK, SURI, KING) as ID outperformance (+0.33%) vs US (-0.71%) signals resilient local demand; momentum is broad but thin, so rotate into names with confirmed volume upticks and avoid chasing COIN/BAUT without earnings confirmation. Position for Q3 staples restocking and rural recovery, targeting 8-12% upside over 4-6 weeks.
